second_order: starting and joining the ace flag and sign
theme_note: These codes hold together because people are beginning a shared mark or adding their own work to its first build: proposing it, placing opening pixels, joining an existing start, writing underneath it, filling purple, or recounting the labour of making it. What varies is whether the contribution is an invitation, a decision to converge on somebody else's start, direct pixel work, or a later account of that work. Grouping review: compared with repair codes after reading all 89 codes; kept here only passages about initiating or joining the build, not the later work of keeping it readable.

second_order: agreeing what the pride sign should say
theme_note: These codes are people settling the public words and layout: asking for one label, joking about what disagreement would spell, choosing the searchable word 'Asexual', agreeing on 'Asexual Pride', and answering what belongs in a blank corner. They vary between explicit agreement, practical explanation, humour that pushes agreement, and a factual design answer. Grouping review: rechecked against neighbour negotiations; these codes decide the ace sign's own wording rather than where another group's art may go.

second_order: keeping the flag and pride letters readable
theme_note: The common practice is repeatedly preserving a recognisable flag or sign while pixels are changed: limiting or enlarging it for maintainability, prioritising letters, recruiting repair, recognising regular defenders, using alternate accounts, restoring damage, and answering or laughing at hostile alterations. What varies is the diagnosis of the interference (trolls, an anti-ace brigade, a claimed attack later denied, or simply wrong pixels), the response (repair, redesign, humour, rest, or calling for help), and assessments from a rare clean screenshot to a losing battle. Grouping review: initially considered separating attacks from repairs, but kept them together because the attack claims are made as part of the same practical work of keeping the sign legible; no code was moved after the review.

second_order: fitting flags, hearts, and neighbours beside one another
theme_note: These exchanges hold together because people are working out spatial coexistence: weaving or merging flags, leaving room for teeth, locating the aro flag, dropping a plan when another group will not turn, moving a heart by one pixel, pairing ace and pan hearts, and refusing a move that would erase Factoria. What varies is whether they accommodate, merge, redirect abandoned space, negotiate colour order, or refuse because their own area has already been cut down. Grouping review: revisited each adjacency code and kept only passages where participants explicitly discuss what should go where; mere reply adjacency was not used.

second_order: bringing in allies and moving planning elsewhere
theme_note: The shared practice is extending the work beyond this subreddit by moving organising to Discord or r/AcePlace and trading repair or protection with Square Spiral and CasualConversation helpers. It varies from a bare redirect, to a reciprocal tile bargain, to reported help from people whose organising remains off record. Grouping review: kept these codes apart from ordinary repair because their distinctive doing is recruiting through another venue or group, not the repair itself.

second_order: feeling proud to see ace work in public
theme_note: These passages make the displayed work meaningful together: people are excited by progress, reproduce it as cross-stitch, celebrate a brief clean view, thank the workers after closing, feel represented, and credit the banner with awareness. The meanings vary from enjoyment and pride to representation and a participant's own claim about awareness; that awareness claim is not treated as a measured effect. Grouping review: separated these codes from building and maintenance because their practice is publicly valuing what the image meant after or alongside the labour.

second_order: rebuilding the banner on the next pixel canvases
theme_note: These codes hold together because people carry the finished r/place design into successor pixel sites: announcing a new start, choosing a non-destructive location, copying the black-on-purple design, starting its A, and pointing from r/AcePlace to Pxls.space. They vary between migration, cautious siting, design replication, and a thin pointer whose deleted body hides the outcome. Grouping review: kept this as a single-code-small practice cluster rather than merging it with the original build, because every passage explicitly acts after /place ended and on a different canvas.
